messages:
liz: quick RFC follow-up — midstream client cancel semantics. if client cancels while upstream is emitting partial tokens, do we: 1) buffer the rest and send trailers, 2) emit trailers immediately with a resume token, or 3) attempt transparent retry to a fallback model? proposing a short 'cancel-grace' window (250ms) and emit a resume-trailer when we stop.
arjun: +1 to discussing tradeoffs. 250ms seems plausible but curious about head-of-line and memory cost if we buffer.
derek: buffering risks hogging slots. my preference: emit trailers immediately with a resume token so client can re-open. keeps gateway stateless for the most part.
mike: if we go resume-token route we need to include: tenant id, model id + version, sequence_offset, kv-cache hash, and an HMAC. otherwise replay/resume attacks are possible.
sophia: agree with mike. also the resume flow must be explicit about eventual consistency: resumed request may return slightly different tokens if model sampling changed. document that in API contract.
liz: sketch of trailer header:

```
Trailer: x-rw-resume-token: base64( {"tenant":"acme","model":"rw-7b-v2","ver":2,"offset":512,"kv_hash":"abc123"} ).hmac
Trailer: x-rw-cancel-grace-ms: 250
```

mike: small nit — include a monotonic request-id in the token so we can tie billing/observability back to original call.
arjun: what about retries vs fallback models? if fallback is used we must ensure side-effect safety (idempotency). proposal: only auto-retry for read-only/generative paths; for tool-calls or webhooks require explicit client retry.
derek: also consider a soft quota: only allow buffering for requests under X tokens to bound memory.
sophia: UX question: clients expect immediate cancel to free connection. if we buffer the gateway still needs to ack cancel to client quickly while doing background resume token generation. that means trailer emission should not block client close.
liz: good point — action items:
- define resume-token payload + HMAC spec @mike
- add cancel-grace config default 250ms with tenant override @arjun
- list auto-retry whitelist (no side-effects) @derek
- document client-visible contract and sampling divergence note @sophia

ops-bot: RFC issue created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/451 :eyes:

mike: :thumbsup: I'll draft the HMAC schema and example code (go/python snippets) — putting a stub in the RFC.
sophia: will add clarifying sentence about sampling divergence and recommended client behavior.
arjun: I'll bake a telemetry experiment to measure how often cancels happen within 250ms vs later.

liz: thanks all, moving this to RFC v2. small follow-up: do we want resumable streaming to be an opt-in header (e.g., `Accept-Resume: true`) so we don't change default behavior for existing clients?
derek: opt-in seems safest.

mike: opt-in + server-side tenant config = good compromise. we can flip default later after data.

liz: cool. closing thread here, will update RFC link when PR has HMAC example.
thread_summary: Discussion on midstream client cancel handling: buffer vs immediate trailer vs auto-retry. proposal: opt-in resumable streaming with a 250ms cancel-grace window, signed resume tokens, tenant overrides, and whitelist for auto-retry.
